title: Artificial Schumann-resonance generator audit for OTA-TEC-0019-2095: Helmholtz field amplitudes, natural Schumann field strength and ELF bioeffect evidence
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0019-2095-DE artificial-Schumann-resonance generator specification, restricted to the real, externally checkable layer the document marks [T]/[S]. Assess: (1) the real-world anchor: verify the Schumann-resonance fundamental near 7.83 Hz and the typical amplitude of the naturally occurring Schumann-resonance magnetic field at Earth's surface (order of magnitude, e.g. pT-range estimates), i.e. what field a habitat generator would need to produce to replicate natural background exposure; (2) internal design arithmetic: does the specified Helmholtz pair (coil diameter 5.0 m, spacing 2.5 m = radius, N = 100 turns, I = 0.5 A AC at 7.83 Hz, 2.0 mm² copper wire, ~10 V) really produce the claimed central field of ~1.8 pT, or does the standard Helmholtz formula B = (8/5√5)·(μ₀·N·I)/R give ~1.8 × 10⁻⁵ T (~18 µT) — i.e. flag the apparent picotesla/microtesla unit inconsistency among the 1.5-2.0 pT design target, the computed central value, the stated field-homogeneity/coverage claims, and the derived ~6.6 W / <10 W power estimate; (3) feasibility: can a ~5 m-diameter, ~10 W, ~500 € copper-wire Helmholtz system realistically deliver the claimed >90 % homogeneity over ~50 m³, and what are the actual trade-offs (wire length ~3.14 km, resistance, voltage, structural support, field falloff outside the central volume); (4) the biological premise: what does the current peer-reviewed evidence (systematic reviews, ELF bioeffect literature, WHO/ICNIRP context) show about biological, sleep or circadian effects of ~7.83 Hz and nearby ELF magnetic fields at pT-µT levels — are artificial 'Schumann-resonance generator' health or sleep claims established, contested, or unsupported, and is the document's precautionary framing ('Selbst wenn Schumann-Bioeffekte minimal sind...') consistent with the evidence; and (5) which wording, figures or [T]/[S]/[F] markers in the document should be narrowed or reclassified. Do NOT validate or alter the fictional 2095-2100 Helios Base evaluation data, sleep-quality/circadian numbers, cost estimates, maintenance claims, or any NOXIA/OTA balancing value. Map supporting, null and constraining evidence without upgrading speculative bioeffect claims to established.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0019-2095 is in the current workqueue (priority 12) and is one of the few queued items whose central engineering claims are presented as real and buildable ('[T] Theoretisch — Physikalisch validiert'; curator note: 'Die Technologie ist real und heute umsetzbar [T]'). Its design parameters contain an internally checkable unit inconsistency (the Helmholtz configuration it specifies cannot produce picotesla fields with microtesla-magnitude arithmetic), and the entire premise rests on the contested scientific status of ELF/Schumann-resonance bioeffects. External physical and biomedical grounding can resolve both, materially improving the spec's internal consistency and its R/T/S/F classification. No prior KUEPER research topic has audited this document or its artificial-Schumann-generator claims.
real_world_anchor: Schumann-resonance phenomenon (7.83 Hz fundamental and natural surface field amplitude), the ELF electromagnetic-field bioeffect literature, and Helmholtz-coil magnetostatic field calculations.
novelty_reason: No prior KUEPER research topic addresses artificial Schumann-resonance generators, Helmholtz-coil field magnitudes, or the ELF/Schumann bioeffect evidence base. The adjacent prior topic RES-20260829-AE1A40C0 concerns 95-120 Hz archaeoacoustic chamber resonance and 110 Hz EEG shifts, which is a different frequency band and evidence domain; RES-20260831-C1748BD0 covers ECLSS alarm thresholds. The 2095 Schumann-generator design arithmetic and its bioeffect premise are a materially new, un-researched dimension.
